new_symbol_range_suggestions.infectious_redundancy_shape: [-1, 5] with 1 + infectious_redundancy_shape*i/(1 + q*i) > 0 over the admissible (q,i) range

derivation_notes: The parent assumes all exposure-acquisition behavior follows one single Hill-type phase. Here that is relaxed by allowing infectious prevalence to alter the saturation shape through a bounded redundancy factor, representing the shift from more independent rare opportunities at low prevalence toward overlapping repeated opportunities at higher prevalence.
change_summary: Added a prevalence-dependent saturation-shape refinement that activates with i and is tempered by total exposure q*i. This changes the input-to-rate mapping directly, allowing different low-i and higher-i approach-to-ceiling behavior than a single Hill family can supply.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: All infectious-contact opportunities are effectively summarized by one homogeneous saturating exposure-response phase, with no additional prevalence-dependent transition between near-independent and redundant contact opportunity sampling.
assumption_audit.mechanism: As infectious prevalence rises, contacts experienced by susceptibles can shift from approximately independent rare opportunities to more redundant repeated opportunities from overlapping infectious sources, changing the shape of saturation itself rather than only the threshold or Hill exponent.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when infectious_redundancy_shape = 0.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed s, the acquisition probability per susceptible is a single Hill-type saturating function of aggregate exposure q*i, with one shared effective threshold and one shared curvature value determined only by linear modulation in s and i.
response_change.child_relation: At fixed s, the exposure-acquisition relation transitions from near-linear response at low infectious prevalence to stronger saturation at higher infectious prevalence because infectious prevalence not only shifts threshold/curvature but also changes how close contact opportunities are to independent across susceptibles, producing a prevalence-dependent saturation shape that cannot be represented by one single-phase Hill form over all i.
response_change.observable_effect: When q and s are held fixed and i is varied from low to moderate values, the child can show a delayed onset of strong saturation at low i but a sharper approach to the contact ceiling at higher i; the parent can only bend this tradeoff through one Hill family and cannot match both low-i near-proportional growth and high-i compressed approach-to-ceiling with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable for 0<s<=1 with q*i spanning below and above the effective half-saturation scale, especially when i varies over a moderate range where repeated or redundant infectious contacts begin to matter but s is not near zero; negligible at very small q*i or i≈0.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, variation in i at fixed s and q can reveal mild deviation from a single Hill phase; in holdout, the same mechanism becomes clearer when q*i extends further into the saturating regime, exposing different low-i versus high-i approach shapes to the same contact ceiling.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added prevalence-dependent shape refinement is set to zero so the exposure-response remains a single Hill-type saturating function with the existing threshold and curvature modulation.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: prevalence-dependent redundancy in infectious opportunity sampling
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: As infectious prevalence rises, contacts experienced by susceptibles can shift from approximately independent rare opportunities to more redundant repeated opportunities from overlapping infectious sources, changing the shape of saturation itself rather than only the threshold or Hill exponent.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the added bounded factor changes the exposure-response shape differently across prevalence regimes, creating an i-dependent departure from a single Hill phase rather than a uniform gain or simple threshold shift.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The current law assumes one single-phase Hill-type acquisition response to aggregate exposure, so infectious prevalence can only alter threshold and exponent smoothly within that same family.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Infectious prevalence also changes the saturation shape through bounded redundancy among infectious opportunities, so the response is no longer confined to one single-phase Hill family.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: s*c*(q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i)/(exposure_half_saturation/((1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s)*(1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i)) + (q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i))
evolution_contract.after_fragment: s*c*(q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i)/(exposure_half_saturation/((1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s)*(1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i)) + (q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i))*(1 + infectious_redundancy_shape*i/(1 + q*i))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The child recovers the parent exactly when infectious_redundancy_shape = 0.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Hold s and q fixed and vary i across a range where q*i moves from below to above the effective half-saturation scale: compared with the parent's single Hill-type family, the child shows an i-dependent reshaping of the rise toward the contact-limited ceiling, weak at very low i and stronger at moderate i where redundancy activates.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot generally absorb this change because the parent only permits i to act through one effective half-saturation factor and one exponent inside a single Hill form. The child introduces a separate bounded prevalence-dependent shape modulation that alters the relation between low-i growth and higher-i approach-to-ceiling at fixed s and q, so fitting the parent to one regime misfits the other when both are sampled.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable for 0<s<=1 with q*i spanning below and above the effective half-saturation scale, especially when i varies over a moderate range where repeated or redundant infectious contacts begin to matter but s is not near zero; negligible at very small q*i or i≈0.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, variation in i at fixed s and q can reveal mild deviation from a single Hill phase; in holdout, the same mechanism becomes clearer when q*i extends further into the saturating regime, exposing different low-i versus high-i approach shapes to the same contact ceiling.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added prevalence-dependent shape refinement is set to zero so the exposure-response remains a single Hill-type saturating function with the existing threshold and curvature modulation.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes one single-phase Hill-type acquisition response to aggregate exposure, so infectious prevalence can only alter threshold and exponent smoothly within that same family.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: All infectious-contact opportunities are effectively summarized by one homogeneous saturating exposure-response phase, with no additional prevalence-dependent transition between near-independent and redundant contact opportunity sampling.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: As infectious prevalence rises, contacts experienced by susceptibles can shift from approximately independent rare opportunities to more redundant repeated opportunities from overlapping infectious sources, changing the shape of saturation itself rather than only the threshold or Hill exponent.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase exposure-response assumption. The parent already lets s and i modulate the threshold and curvature, but it still forces all observations onto one Hill-type saturating family. Vary i while holding s and q fixed, over admissible 0<=i<=1 with q*i crossing the effective half-saturation region. Under the child mechanism, low i corresponds to more nearly independent infectious opportunities and therefore a more gradual early rise, whereas higher i creates more redundant overlap and a more compressed final approach to the same finite contact-limited ceiling. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the instantaneous new_infection_rate versus supplied inputs changes directly. A single refit of the parent parameters may mimic part of this behavior locally, but cannot generally match both the low-i and higher-i shape regimes simultaneously when both are present in the sampled domain. The effect is scientifically limited if data stay entirely in the unsaturated low-exposure regime or if i remains extremely small, where both parent and child collapse toward approximately linear dependence on q*i.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: Estimate the instantaneous rate at which susceptible people acquire infection under independently sampled contact and infectiousness conditions. The baseline mechanism is infectious contact generation with a contact-limited acquisition response that approaches a finite ceiling at high exposure. Susceptibility and infectious prevalence are treated as externally specified conditions rather than evolving states. The output is an instantaneous epidemiological rate, so no time integration is required.
